definition: A swift witness is a person who testifies hastily or eagerly, often before having full knowledge of the facts. A swift witness is generally viewed as unreliable because their testimony is given without sufficient reflection. In legal proceedings, a swift witness may be contrasted with a credible or impartial witness. Their eagerness to testify, especially when motivated by personal interest or emotion, can suggest bias or lack of candor. Courts and juries often weigh such testimony with caution.
